findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @reclaimprotocol/agent
findings.detail: 'reclaimprotocol__agent' launches @reclaimprotocol/agent through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@reclaimprotocol/agent@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): check_attestor
findings.detail: The description of 'reclaimprotocol__agent.check_attestor' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: concealment. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: concealment, entropy, log_len.

evidence.description: Checks that the Reclaim attestor works from this machine by proving a public CoinGecko price request with a throwaway key. It uses no credential, provider, or logged-in site, and takes up to 45 seconds (about 8 when healthy). Call it once when you set up a new provider build, and after `run_proof` fails with a network error. findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description:
Create an organization

Creates a new `ORG`-kind organization with the caller as its first `OWNER`. Every user gets a default organization at sign-up, and it counts toward their org-creation limit (1 active organization unless Reclaim support raises it). Past the limit this returns `409`; contact support@reclaimprotocol.org to raise the limit or archive an organization.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'reclaimprotocol__agent': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 54 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'reclaimprotocol__agent': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 90 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
